title: Spare Parts by David J. Glass at Theatre Row #sparepartsplay #theatre...
transcript: This play felt like a Black Mirror episode, but without the urgency. It's about a billionaire who's willing to invest whatever it takes to reverse the aging process, much to the concern of some researchers at Columbia University. The plot is too realistic to be completely dystopian but too far fetched in its details to take place “tomorrow” as indicated in the program. I couldn't quite decipher in which way I was to interpret it, so it was never fully satisfying, even with its well-constructed dramatic stakes. The revelations are often entertaining or humorous, but they undermine the ethical questions that the play raises regarding human experimentation. And despite the solid performances from the entire cast, the characters feel overly functional to the plot, rather than free agents within it, so the play ends up feeling stiff and too contrived to meaningfully engage with the ethical dilemmas it intends to invoke. I think if science fiction thrillers are your thing, this play still has a lot to offer. I was certainly intrigued by the premise and riveted by the way it concluded — I just couldn't shake the amount of unforced errors in the writing up to that point. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer identifies solid performances and an intriguing premise but repeatedly criticizes the writing as contrived, stiff, and unsatisfying, undermining the ethical stakes. The soft recommendation is conditional on genre fans, not a general endorsement.
